notes: §1985:XIII.4.2.2 is `CLOSE {file-name-1 [{REEL | UNIT} [FOR REMOVAL] | WITH {NO REWIND | LOCK}]}...` for a report file, the WITH LOCK alternative being the one 2023 dropped. The grammar closeOption admits exactly those alternatives (WITH, FOR optional words, REMOVAL only after REEL/UNIT), BindClose resolves each report file-name (admitsReportFile) and maps the written option to BoundCloseKind.WithLock/ReelUnit/ReelUnitForRemoval/NoRewind, and VersionConformancePass.VisitCloseOption gates LOCK only from 2023 (CloseWithLockRemoved2023), so 85 accepts it. Probes at --std 85 with FILE STATUS FS: witness CLOSE ... WITH LOCK prints CLOSED; (e) CLOSE WITH LOCK gives 00 and a following OPEN OUTPUT gives 38 (Table 1 E, file locked); CLOSE REEL and CLOSE UNIT FOR REMOVAL of the disk report file give 07 and the file stays open (GENERATE afterwards works, Table 1 F); CLOSE NO REWIND gives 07; CLOSE and CLOSE LOCK of an unopened file give 42; (b) `WITH LOCK REEL` COBOL2269, `REMOVAL` without REEL COBOL2269, `CLOSE.` with zero operands COBOL0001; the same file twice closes then gives 42. (c) the 2023 form adds nothing to CLOSE for 85 to refuse. (a)(d)(f) do not reach a file-name list.

next.reason: 1985: "WITH ╭ NO REWIND╮ ┤ ├ ╰ LOCK ╯"; 2023: "WITH NO REWIND (no LOCK alternative in the 2023 CLOSE format)". The CLOSE format is carried with {REEL|UNIT} [FOR REMOVAL] and WITH NO REWIND, but the WITH LOCK alternative is gone, so CLOSE file WITH LOCK is no longer accepted.
